title: Dominic and the Static
premise: Isandro Coldharbour, navigator of the derelict freighter Ox-Alpha, has spent eleven years orbiting the dead colony of Meridian, secretly recording its decay while the cryo-hold sleeps with two thousand colonists—only half of whom can ever be revived. When gravity stutters across the system for nine seconds, Isandro realizes someone out there is still watching, and that their long invisibility has ended. As a salvage fleet closes in to strip the colony and its sleepers, Isandro must choose which half of humanity wakes, forging an uneasy alliance with the colony's last living survivor, a girl named Wren who was born after everyone forgot. In the end, Isandro sacrifices their own recorded identity—the only proof they ever existed—to broadcast the truth and wake the children's half of the hold, escaping into the dark as something new: unnamed, unrecorded, and finally free.
about_author: Sebastian Kavanagh is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years stationed on remote North Atlantic platforms before turning to fiction. He writes science fiction about people the systems forgot, from a farmhouse in Newfoundland where the static never quite stops.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. During a routine navigation check, gravity across the entire Meridian system flickers for exactly nine seconds, waking every alarm aboard the Ox-Alpha at once. Isandro logs it, lies about it in the official record, and realizes someone else is out there. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Hold Below
chapters.summary: Isandro descends into the cryo-hold among the sleeping backups—colonists whose minds were copied before launch—and reveals through memory fragments why they fled Earth and why only half can wake. Emotional beat: guilt as a physical place you can walk through.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the surface, seventeen-year-old Wren—the colony's last living child, born after the abandonment—detects the ship that has orbited her whole life and sends a signal no one has sent in years. Emotional beat: furious hope.

chapters.title: Contact Protocol
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Against protocol, Isandro answers Wren's signal and learns the colony wasn't evacuated—it was written off, its death filed as an accounting error. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering your survival was someone else's paperwork.

chapters.title: The Salvage Charter
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A corporate salvage fleet enters the system under a charter claiming everything, including the cryo-hold's 'assets.' Isandro must decide whether to run or stand, while Wren shows them what remains worth saving. Emotional beat: the law arrives as a threat.

chapters.title: What the Static Says
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Decoding old colony transmissions, Wren and Isandro discover the nine-second gravity flicker was a handshake—a rescue attempt by descendants of the first colonists, thought lost. Emotional beat: grief complicated by the possibility it wasn't too late after all.

chapters.title: Half a Humanity
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The revival systems can only sustain one thousand sleepers. Isandro drafts the selection criteria alone at night, confronting the backups—who are them, in a sense—and the arithmetic of playing god. Emotional beat: the loneliest decision ever made.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Salvage marines board the Ox-Alpha; Wren creates a diversion from the surface using the colony's dying power grid, buying Isandro hours to begin the revivals. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Climax. Isandro wipes their own identity records and broadcasts the full archive of the colony's abandonment to the rescuers' fleet, trading their existence for the truth. The chosen thousand wake as the marines breach the hold. Emotional beat: self-erasure as the ultimate act of witness.

chapters.title: Coldharbour, Empty
chapters.summary: Resolution. Wren's POV, months later: the awakened colonists rebuild above while the rescuers' ships carry the archive home. A navigator with no name and no record pilots the Ox-Alpha out of the system, answering to nothing but the static. Emotional beat: freedom that costs everything, and is worth it.
